key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXenes are chemically unstable in halide perovskite precursor inks, but the extent and direction of surface change depend strongly on which precursor species they encounter.
engineering_relevance: MXene-based perovskite devices must control ink composition and mixing order because iodine species can destroy flakes, while MAI can passivate and help preserve their surface.
method: XPS tracked MXene surface chemistry after exposure to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
DFT identified adsorption and oxidation pathways for I2, polyiodides, Pb2+, and MAI on Ti3C2Tx surfaces.
Comparative analysis separated aggressive oxidizers from stabilizing adsorbates and linked effects to precursor sequence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a combined XPS and DFT study showing rapid MXene degradation with I2/polyiodides, slower oxidation with PbI2, and stabilization with MAI, including sequence-dependent surface evolution.
watch_item: Results are based on a model MAPbI3 precursor system, so behavior may vary with different perovskite chemistries, solvent conditions, or processing sequences.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
